entries.source: Syllogsim 02  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 4
entries.question: Coded syllogism
entries.explanation: The coded statement guarantees some Dream are Experience, only a few Experience are happy, and some happy are horrible. It does not force Experience to overlap horrible; Dream–horrible overlap remains possible under the stated relations, so only I follows.

entries.source: Syllogsim 02  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 6
entries.question: Reverse syllogism
entries.explanation: Option C says all ice are tea and some drinks are ice; therefore some tea are drink. It places no restriction that forces water to overlap ice, so their non-overlap remains possible. The other sets do not establish both conclusions.

entries.source: Syllogsim 02  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 7
entries.question: Reverse syllogism
entries.explanation: Option D gives some iron that are pots and states no metal is iron, so that existing iron is not metal. All pots are aluminium, making that same existing iron also aluminium and not metal; both conclusions follow.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 8, Q30
entries.question: Q30
entries.explanation: At least a few B are D, and all B are C, establishing some C–D overlap. The source uses ‘at least few’ as a non-universal few relation, so some C are D and some C are not D; conclusion II follows. No relation establishes I or the impossibility asserted in III.
entries.reason: ‘At least few B are D’ guarantees some B∩D but does not prove some C outside D; therefore ‘Very few C are D’ is not established.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 9, Q31
entries.question: Q31
entries.explanation: The statements do not force every fruit-orange overlap into Apple, so a fruit outside Apple is possible and I follows as a possibility. No statement guarantees an orange outside Mango, so II does not follow.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 10, Q32
entries.question: Q32
entries.explanation: ‘Only a few bats are cats’ guarantees some bats outside cats, so II follows. Rats are a subset of bats and may occupy the non-cat region; the source’s ‘can not’ possibility wording makes I possible as well. Both follow.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 11, Q33
entries.question: Q33
entries.explanation: The statements do not force neighbours to overlap cool, so some of the neighbour group can be outside cool; I is possible. The existing cool boys could all be good, so II is not definite.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 12, Q34
entries.question: Q34
entries.explanation: Only a few windows are gates guarantees some window-gates. Since no rod is a gate, those windows cannot be rods, establishing I. Nothing establishes existence of a rod outside windows, so II does not follow.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 13, Q35
entries.question: Q35
entries.explanation: The bird-cat existence does not prevent additional cats outside birds, so I is possible. No plant is a bird makes any plants non-birds, but plant existence is not given, so the existential ‘very few’ conclusion II does not follow.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 14, Q36
entries.question: Q36
entries.explanation: Some ships are submarines, but no statement forces ships to be planes; placing the existing ship-boat outside planes is possible, so I follows. The universal claim that all ships are not planes is not established.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 15, Q43
entries.question: Q43
entries.explanation: Only a few D are C ensures some D lie outside C; since B is within C, those D are not B, so II follows. The D∩C portion is not forced outside A, so I does not follow.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 16, Q44
entries.question: Q44
entries.explanation: The deer-goat existence does not force goats into dogs. The dog-deer overlap guaranteed by ‘only a few’ does not require cats to exist or overlap deer. Neither conclusion follows.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 17, Q45
entries.question: Q45
entries.explanation: I contradicts the separation of pencils and books. ‘Only a few books are copies’ guarantees some book-copy overlap; since no pencil is a book, those copies are not pencils, so II follows.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 19, Q47
entries.question: Q47
entries.explanation: Only a few pets are cats guarantees some pets outside cats, so I follows. Bats are only known to be pets; their overlap with cats is not required, so II does not follow.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 20, Q48
entries.question: Q48
entries.explanation: ‘Almost all tables are chairs’ guarantees some table-chair members; all chairs are desks, so I follows. The wood-table members are not guaranteed to lie in the chair portion, so II is not forced.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 21, Q49
entries.question: Q49
entries.explanation: C and D overlap, but F can overlap C outside E because only E is excluded from C; thus I is not forced. The C-D overlap need not intersect F, so II is not forced. Neither follows.

entries.source: Syllogsim 03  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 22, Q50
entries.question: Q50
entries.explanation: Cats are within black, while ants are within red. The overlap of ant and cat is not specified; neither a nonempty overlap nor a complete separation is forced. Neither conclusion follows.

entries.question: reverse syllogism, auto/equine/slides
entries.reason: None of the listed statement sets entails both supplied conclusions.

new_original_practice_questions.question:
For this question, use classical categorical logic: universal statements carry no existential import; ‘some’ asserts existence; and ‘only a few X are Y’ means both that some X are Y and that some X are not Y. Possibility is assessed by whether at least one model satisfies it.
Statements:
1. All analysts are auditors.
2. No analysts are auditors.
Conclusions:
I. All analysts are auditors.
II. No analysts are auditors.
Which conclusion(s) logically follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II follows

new_original_practice_questions.independent_reasoning: All analysts are auditors; No analysts are auditors. Exhaustive three-set Venn-region checking leaves 15 nonempty models consistent with the statements. Conclusion I is true in every such model; conclusion II is true in every such model. Thus both conclusions follow.
